blocks.html: Get protected in about 5 minutes. Click a step to see the details.

items.title: Install a private browser
items.text: Pick Brave, Mullvad Browser, or LibreWolf and set it as your default. See Part 1: Choose Your Browser for the full picture, including a two- or three-browser lineup.

items.title: Install one extension
items.text: Install uBlock Origin — verify the developer is Raymond Hill (gorhill). It’s the single most effective privacy tool you can add. Full walkthrough in Part 2: Set Up Your Browser.

items.title: Turn on strict tracking protection
items.text: Firefox/LibreWolf: Enhanced Tracking Protection → Strict. Brave: Shields set to Aggressive. This also cuts down fingerprinting — see Part 3: Advanced Configurations for browser-specific detail.

items.title: Verify it’s working
items.text: Visit coveryourtracks.eff.org and confirm strong tracking protection. Full test suite in Part 4: Test & Verify.

subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: Your browser is the window you use to see almost everything online — and the window works both ways. Websites, advertisers and trackers can read a lot about you through it: what you visit, what you click, and enough details about your device to recognise you again later. Choosing a private browser and setting it up well removes most of that tracking without changing how you use the web.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: Tracker
items.html: A script or pixel from a third party (often an ad company) that follows you from site to site.

items.title: Cookie
items.html: A small file a site stores in your browser. Useful for logins, but third-party cookies are used for tracking.

items.title: Fingerprinting
items.html: Identifying your browser from its unique mix of settings, fonts, screen size and hardware, without cookies.

items.title: Extension
items.html: An add-on that changes what your browser does, like an ad blocker. Each one can also see your browsing.

items.title: Global Privacy Control (GPC)
items.html: A signal your browser sends telling sites not to sell or share your data.

items.title: Chromium / Gecko
items.html: The two main browser engines. Chrome, Brave and Edge use Chromium; Firefox and LibreWolf use Gecko.

lede: The step-by-step guide that actually works — four short parts, no jargon, five minutes to get meaningfully protected.
